method: Instruction listings decoded directly from the PE bytes of the identified executable through its section table, with the executable size and SHA-256 verified first. Every cited instruction address, operand, name literal, holder vftable cell, jump table entry and call target was compared with those listings by a second pass that re-read the bytes. Callers were enumerated by scanning the .text section for rel32 call and jmp instructions, so virtual and indirect callers are not covered. Addresses are absolute virtual addresses. The MEASURED facts are call-site and chunk counts that agree with xivl-client-scripts:lua/napi_index.json and scans of the executable named in each fact. Script argument counts, constants and calling function names come from a local Lua 5.1 bytecode scan that no tracked artifact carries and are INFERRED. No decompiled body is a tracked evidence dependency.
scope: Static Lua call contracts of eleven native registrations: _hasItemPackage, _isActorMainStatMode, _lockTargetCursorControl, _unlockTargetCursorControl, _isTargetCursorControlEnabled, _isInn, _getLocalizedDisplayName, _getLocalizedDisplayNameForChat, _isTalkable, _isEmotable and _isPushable. Four PlayerBase command natives (_executeCommand, _canExecuteCommand, _cancelCommand and _isCommandPlaying) are carried as dispatch rows. Each row gives the registration site, receiver type check, declared argument and return lists, reads, client state effects, failure behavior and yield behavior. Client-side contracts do not establish package numbers, main stat values, display names, inn areas or server behavior.
evidenceTier: MIXED, see tierVocabulary and the tier of each fact

framework.reference: manifests/nameplate_group_native_call_contract.json framework and manifests/work_binder_native_call_contract.json framework: registration, the 0x00CC9D60 type registry, argument marshalling through 0x00D19A20, the holder receiver adapter, the cell tags, the invalid-parameter route, the return pushers and the world object chain. Each registrar builds the return list first and the argument list second.

registration.note: The order of a native is its position among the rel32 calls of its switchboard, counted from 1. Each registrar has one rel32 caller in .text, recorded as registrarCaller. The first call of a registrar builds the return list and the second builds the argument list.

framework.holdersNote: Each invoke routine casts the receiver with 0x009DA6CC from LuaControl (0x01270B4C) to the target type descriptor. A null cast returns false without calling the callback.

argumentReaders.0x005819A0: int, cell tag 0. A mismatched tag reaches 0x00CCA730.

listBuilders.note: The builders select registry entries by position: entry 0 int, entry 2 bool, entry 3 Utf8String and entry 4 LuaControl*, as in manifests/work_binder_native_call_contract.json.

returnPushers.0x00748870: bool, cell tag 2. 0x00583E30 copies one byte through the pointer.

worldObject.chain: R is the address that 0x00CC7510 returns for ExecuteParameters +0x04. X = [R], Y = [X +0x04], W = [Y] and V = [W], the chain of manifests/global_native_call_contract.json.

fields.Y +0x08: Object whose first dword is V. The target cursor natives pass it to the glue routines 0x0075B270, 0x0075B280 and 0x0075B290.
fields.Y +0xDC: Value whose first dword addresses the object that _getLocalizedDisplayNameForChat calls through virtual slot 5.

worldObject.tier: STATIC for the offsets and calls, INFERRED for the roles.

framework.invalidParameterRoute: A failed cell vector size test calls 0x009D22B4. The target cursor contract records that routine as the invalid-parameter route that ends in TerminateProcess.

raptureUserControl.records: Four 0x14 byte records at object +0x08, each initialized by 0x004DEC70 with 0 at record +0x10. The counters are the dwords at object +0x18, +0x2C, +0x40 and +0x54.
raptureUserControl.tier: STATIC. Slots 1, 2, 7 and 8 are recorded in manifests/binding_map_native_call_contract.json and manifests/work_binder_native_call_contract.json.

returns.note: True when the item package manager of the receiver holds a nonzero record under the key package number minus 1.

rows.behavior: Reads a 1-based package number, looks key minus 1 up in the package tree of the item package manager at receiver +0xD8 and pushes true when the record pointer found is nonzero. The manager is created on first use. An absent package pushes false. It requests no yield and writes no state other than that lazy creation.

facts.claim: The callback builds a helper object through 0x006DD450, calls the body 0x00702880 with the ExecuteParameters pointer, the receiver and that helper as ecx, and destroys the helper through 0x006DD4D0. The body never reads its ecx before overwriting it, so the helper is inert for this native.

The body tests the cell vector size. The vector record is the dword at +0x04 of the holder at ExecuteParameters +0x10, its start dword is at +0x04 and its end dword at +0x08, and a cell is 16 bytes. An empty vector calls 0x009D22B4. It reads cell 0 through the int reader 0x005819A0, whose tag mismatch reaches 0x00CCA730.
It subtracts 1 through 0x0078BC90 (add eax, -1) with no range test, so the package number 0 searches the key 0xFFFFFFFF.

0x006F51A0 on the receiver returns the dword at receiver +0xD8. When it is null the routine allocates 0x78 bytes through 0x009D1B35, constructs the manager with 0x006F5100 and stores the pointer at +0xD8. The CharaBase control constructor stores 0 at +0xD8.

0x006E5BA0 searches the tree at manager +0x08 for the key through 0x0071D420, which walks to the first node not below the key by unsigned compares and reports the end when the key is below that node. It returns the dword at node +0x10, or 0 for the end node.
A nonzero result pushes true and zero pushes false through the bool pusher 0x00748870 with the return container at ExecuteParameters +0x1C.
The shipped scripts contain 19 call sites in 13 chunks. The counts agree with xivl-client-scripts:lua/napi_index.json.

Each of the 19 sites passes one argument and six of them pass the constant 100. The other sites pass a variable. This comes from a local Lua 5.1 bytecode scan of the installed scripts with tools/decode_lpb.py. No tracked artifact carries argument counts, constants or calling function names.
The key is the package number minus 1 and the record is the item package of that number. That role comes from the native name and from the shared lookup of _getItemPackageFreeSpace.
The writers of the package tree, the package numbers that exist for a given receiver and the value of a record under a key were not traced.

arguments.note: Mode bit. Only the exact values 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64 and 128 select a group.

returns.note: True when the main stat dword of the actor belongs to the group that the mode argument selects.

rows.behavior: Reads one int mode, resolves the receiver identity to its chara record, loads the main stat dword at chara +0xF0 and pushes whether that dword is a member of the group that the mode selects through 0x0078E0E0. Any other mode value pushes false. It requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback tests the cell vector size, reads cell 0 as an int through 0x005819A0 and keeps it in edi. An empty vector calls 0x009D22B4.

It reaches the world chain through 0x00CC7510 on ExecuteParameters +0x04, loads the receiver identity from +0x0C and calls 0x0075C1B0 on W. That routine resolves the identity through 0x004D9970 and 0x004DE190 and calls 0x00585400, which loads the dword at chara +0xF0. The identity 0xC0000000 and an absent identity resolve to 0, and no instruction tests the pointer before the load.
It calls 0x0078E0E0 with the Lua int as the first stdcall argument and the stat as the second, stores the returned al and pushes it through the bool pusher 0x00748870.

0x0078E0E0 subtracts 1 from the mode and sends a result above 0x7F, as an unsigned compare, to the false exit 0x0078E12E. Otherwise the byte table at 0x0078E1A0 selects one of nine jump targets from the table at 0x0078E17C. The table indexes 0, 1, 3, 7, 15, 31, 63 and 127 select cases 0 to 7 and every other index selects case 8, the false exit. So only the single bit values 1 to 128 reach a case and a sum of bits pushes false.

The eight cases test the stat as follows. Mode 1: 1 or 3. Mode 2: 2 or 0x51. Mode 4: 0x1E to 0x20. Mode 8: 0x32 or 0x33. Mode 16: 0x46. Mode 32: 0x0B, 0x0D or 0x0E through the helper 0x0078E090. Mode 64: 0x0C. Mode 128: 0x0F or 0x5B. A stat outside the selected set pushes false.
The shipped scripts contain 8 call sites in 4 chunks. The counts agree with xivl-client-scripts:lua/napi_index.json.

Each site passes one argument. CharaBaseClass.isDeadMode passes 1, isSitMode passes 32, isActiveMode passes 2, 4, 8 and 16 in turn and stops at the first true, and the talk command passes 2. No shipped script passes 64 or 128. This comes from a local Lua 5.1 bytecode scan of the installed scripts with tools/decode_lpb.py. No tracked artifact carries argument counts, constants or calling function names.
The stat dword is the actor main stat that _getActorMainStat returns. The group names dead, active and sit come from the script helper names, not from the executable.

The writers of the dword at chara +0xF0, the names of the stat values and the roles of modes 64 and 128 were not traced. The run-time result for a receiver that is absent from the identity registry was not observed.

rows.behavior: Takes no argument and adds 1 to the target cursor control counter, the dword at +0x2C of the RaptureUserControl object. It pushes no value and requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback reads the world chain through 0x00CC7510, loads the dword at Y +0x08 and calls 0x0075B270. That glue loads V, calls 0x004D7580, which adds 0x17758 to V, and tail jumps through virtual slot 4 of the object at that address.

The object has the vftable 0x00F90F64 with the RTTI name Application::Main::SqwtInterface::RaptureUserControl. Slot 4 is 0x0054B620, which adds 1 to the dword at object +0x2C and returns the new value. The value is not tested, bounded or pushed.

The constructor 0x004DECF0 builds four 0x14 byte records at object +0x08 through 0x004DEC70, and 0x004DEC70 stores 0 in the dword at record +0x10. The counter at object +0x2C is the dword at +0x10 of record 1, so it starts at 0.
The engine calls the same glue directly at 0x0070402D, next to the player control glue 0x0075B240 at 0x00704026.
The shipped scripts contain 12 call sites in 5 chunks. The counts agree with xivl-client-scripts:lua/napi_index.json.

No site passes an argument. PlayerBaseClass._onPreEvent and _onPreCommand call it and DesktopWidget.setTutorialMask calls it together with _unlockTargetCursorControl. The opening quest scripts man0g0, man0l0 and man0u0 contain the other sites. This comes from a local Lua 5.1 bytecode scan of the installed scripts with tools/decode_lpb.py. No tracked artifact carries argument counts, constants or calling function names.
The counter is a lock count that suppresses target cursor input while it is above 0. That role comes from the native names and from the paired use in _isTargetCursorControlEnabled.
The consumers of the counter other than the three natives and the engine call sites were not traced.

rows.behavior: Takes no argument and subtracts 1 from the target cursor control counter only when the counter is above 0. It pushes no value and requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback reaches the object at V +0x17758 as _lockTargetCursorControl does. It calls 0x0075B290, which tail jumps through virtual slot 6 and returns the dword at object +0x2C. A value of 0 or below, as a signed compare, ends the call.
A positive value calls 0x0075B280, which tail jumps through virtual slot 5. Slot 5 is 0x0054B630, which adds -1 to the dword at object +0x2C.

The engine calls the slot 5 glue directly at 0x00703A7E, next to the player control glue 0x0075B250 at 0x00703A77. Slot 5 (0x0054B630) is an unconditional add of -1 with no test of the counter, so the engine unlock is not guarded and the counter can go negative.

returns.note: The record Utf8String, or the text that the macro <fixed(21,id)> resolves to.

rows.behavior: Takes no argument. When the id dword at the start of the display name record at receiver +0x60 is -1 it pushes the record Utf8String as _getLocalizedDisplayName does. Otherwise it formats the text <fixed(21,id)>, resolves it through a virtual call on the object at Y +0xDC and pushes the resulting Utf8String. It requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback loads the dword at receiver +0x60 and compares the dword it addresses with -1. Equal takes the direct branch, which pushes the string at record +0x04 through 0x007487C0.

Otherwise it reads the world chain through 0x00CC7510, loads the dword at Y +0xDC and calls 0x0075D020 with a Utf8String result slot and the id. That routine formats the id into a 0x40 byte buffer with the format string at 0x00FDF6BC, which is <fixed(21,%d)>, loads the object that the first dword of the +0xDC value addresses and calls its virtual slot 5 (offset 0x14) with the result string and the buffer. The result string is pushed through 0x007487C0 and then destroyed.
No instruction tests the dword at +0x60, which the CharaBase control constructor stores as 0.

A first dword other than -1 is a sheet index and the branch resolves it to a name. The role comes from the shape of the branches and from the _getDisplayName record in manifests/binding_map_native_call_contract.json.
The shipped scripts contain 2 call sites in 1 chunk, the desktop widget connector. The counts agree with xivl-client-scripts:lua/napi_index.json.

arguments.note: One list entry is declared by 0x0072C260, but the callback is not tolerant of its absence. Past the empty-vector exit, a call with no argument cell reaches the invalid-parameter route 0x009D22B4. The control in the cell is never consulted.

rows.behavior: Reads the raw first cell of the argument list and the pointer vector at receiver +0xE8. An empty vector pushes false before the cell vector is read. With a non-empty vector and no argument cell, the invalid-parameter route 0x009D22B4 is called. A first cell whose tag is not 4 pushes true. A first cell with tag 4 pushes true when some element of the vector has the byte at element +0x58 equal to the byte at 0x012C3F77. The control in the cell is not consulted. It requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback passes the address of receiver +0xE8 and the cell vector holder at ExecuteParameters +0x10 to 0x0071DE70 and pushes the returned al through the bool pusher 0x00748870 with the return container at ExecuteParameters +0x1C.

0x0071DE70 returns false when the vector at +0x04 and +0x08 of its first argument holds no 4 byte element, before it reads the cell vector. Otherwise it tests the cell vector size, which is counted in 16 byte cells, and calls 0x009D22B4 at 0x0071DEA3 when the vector is empty. It then returns true when the byte at +0x0C of cell 0 is not 4.

A script call with no argument leaves the cell vector empty, so on a receiver whose vector is non-empty the call reaches 0x009D22B4, and on a receiver whose vector is empty it pushes false. The shipped scripts contain call sites with no argument for this native (see the call site fact). Whether the executor adds cells for a declared argument that the call omits, and what the invalid-parameter route does for this callback, were not run.

For tag 4 it calls 0x0071DA00, which scans the elements from the start for the first whose byte at +0x58 equals the byte at 0x012C3F77 and returns it, or 0. The routine ignores its argument, so the identity of the control in the cell does not matter. The result is tested for nonzero.

The shipped scripts contain 5 call sites in 3 chunks. The chunks are the desktop widget connector, the depiction judge and a debug command chunk. The counts agree with xivl-client-scripts:lua/napi_index.json.

The argument counts are {"0": 2, "1": 2, "open": 1}. This comes from a local Lua 5.1 bytecode scan of the installed scripts with tools/decode_lpb.py. No tracked artifact carries argument counts, constants or calling function names.
The writers of the vector, the class of its elements, the role of the byte at +0x58 and the writer of the byte at 0x012C3F77 were not traced.

dispatch.thunk: mov eax,[ecx], mov eax,[eax+0xA8], jmp eax

relatedNatives.note: The callback is a three instruction thunk through slot 0xA8 of the receiver vftable. The PlayerBase cell holds 0x006DE8A0, which is a bare ret 4 and pushes nothing, so a PlayerBase receiver that is not a MyPlayer pushes no value. The MyPlayer cell holds 0x0070A010. The MyPlayer routine 0x0070A010 compares receiver +0x128 and +0x12C with the dword at 0x0130C778 and otherwise reads the argument cells. Its body was not traced further.

dispatch.thunk: mov eax,[ecx], mov eax,[eax+0xBC], jmp eax

relatedNatives.note: The callback is a three instruction thunk through slot 0xBC of the receiver vftable. The PlayerBase cell holds 0x006DE8F0, which is a bare ret 4 and pushes nothing, so a PlayerBase receiver that is not a MyPlayer pushes no value. The MyPlayer cell holds 0x00704AA0.
